record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons
record.original_question: Find a polynomial-time algorithm that constructs a covering set for a visibility graph matching the optimal asymptotic bit bound.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 43 Find a covering set which matches the above bound in polynomial time.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P be a simple polygon with n vertices, and let G be its vertex visibility graph: the graph on the vertex set of P in which two vertices are adjacent if and only if the open line segment joining them lies in the closure of the interior of P (so adjacencies include polygon edges as well as interior diagonals).

A Hamiltonian cycle C of G that traverses the vertices of P in their cyclic order along the boundary is called the boundary cycle. An ordered chord of C is a chord (u,v) of C together with a chosen direction. A covering set for G (with respect to C) is a collection S of ordered chords of C such that every chord of C lies in the convex hull, in the appropriate combinatorial sense induced by the boundary cycle, of some ordered chord in S; equivalently, S certifies one of the standard necessary conditions of Ghosh for a graph to be the visibility graph of a simple polygon, namely that every chord of the Hamiltonian boundary cycle is "covered" by some member of S.

It is known that there exist covering sets whose total descriptive size, measured in bits, matches a certain optimal asymptotic upper bound f(n) (the best presently established information-theoretic bound on the size of a smallest covering set for an n-vertex visibility graph).

Problem. Design an algorithm that, given as input the visibility graph G on n vertices together with its boundary Hamiltonian cycle C, runs in time polynomial in n and outputs a covering set for G whose total bit-size is O(f(n)), thereby matching the optimal asymptotic bit bound in polynomial time.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search for a polynomial-time construction of an optimal-size covering set for visibility graphs of simple polygons did not return any publication that resolves this question. Surveys and follow-up work on visibility-graph recognition continue to list polynomial-time testability of Ghosh's higher necessary conditions (which involve covering sets) as unresolved, but no source explicitly confirms that this specific covering-set construction problem has been settled. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

status_evidence.title: On recognizing and characterizing visibility graphs of simple polygons
status_evidence.snippet: It remains open whether the third and fourth necessary conditions of Ghosh can be tested in polynomial time.
status_evidence.claim: Polynomial-time tractability of the necessary conditions involving covering sets is still listed as open.
